text:
Alex: heads up — after the last canary we saw host CPU spike ~2.3x on the ingress parse path during streaming requests. p95 latency +~40ms. repro on canary host 10.2.4.7
Sasha: ack. did you capture a flamegraph?
Alex: yes: https://flame.internal/runs/1795-frag-preparse (private)
Devon: raw pprof snippet from the host: ```
parse_frame+0x1a3   42.1%
writev_coalesce+0x7f 25.4%
kv_cache_lookup       10.2%
sys_sendmsg            7.3%
```
Priya: that looks like repeated small-write path + parser allocations. frameless parsing mode + small client chunks -> lots of reallocs.
Sasha: also seeing more syscalls (sendmsg/sendto) in the trace, suggests fragmentation at http/gRPC layer. windowing + small frames.
Devon: I repro'd locally with a streaming client that sends 512B chunks — CPU jumps and host parse allocs skyrocket.
Alex: stack extract: ```
0x7f12 parse_frame alloc_buffer
0x8b3  parse_frame append_chunk -> grow_by(256)
0x5c0  writev_coalesce flush_small_writes
```
Priya: quick idea: prealloc an 8k buffer for the parser in the fast-path so small frames don't trigger repeated growth.
Sasha: we should try toggling the frameless flag too; for smallpayload clients frameless seems worse.
Devon: i can push a canary patch for prealloc + bump the writev threshold from 128 -> 1024 bytes. will run microbench.
Alex: mitigation note: for canary set config: `ingress.parser.prealloc=8192` and `ingress.coalesce.min_write=1024`.
ci-bot: deploy started for canary/host/1795004330 at 2026-03-19T18:05:30Z
Priya: quick bench after patch: p95 latency decreased ~22ms, host parse CPU down ~30% on the canary region. still seeing small tail spikes at high QPS.
Sasha: interesting — maybe KV cache behavior exacerbates this. low KV hit-rate means we do more parse work per request. add kv hit histogram to the metric set.
Devon: added a perf run (ab-style) that simulates 512B streaming messages across 200 concurrent streams. gist: https://gists.internal/1795/repro.md
Alex: long-term work: 1) smarter coalescer with time-based coalesce (hold 200us before flush) 2) parse prealloc by common client profile 3) tune http2 windowing for streaming clients 4) add metric for parse.allocs + kv.hit-rate correlation
Priya: also consider kernel-selection/batching side effects — parser jitter may cause runtime to generate smaller minibatches, hurting GPU utilization. add a synthetic test that measures batch size distribution under parse load.
Sasha: agreed. will pair with infra to add batch histogram in the pipeline.
Devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/1234 — includes prealloc + coalesce threshold + tests.
Alex: will run canary for 2 hours, then roll to staging if stable. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sasha: nice triage. can we also add a small README in the repo on how to reproduce the fragmentation locally? saves future time.
Devon: adding repro steps to PR.
Priya: followups: add kv histograms, batch-size distribution test, and evaluate frameless mode defaults.
Alex: tracking tickets: RD-3128 (prealloc canary), RD-3130 (kv histograms), RD-3131 (batch-dist test). I'll link them in the PR.
Sasha: cool. keep an eye on the canary traces, ping if tail climbs again.
